text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a p95 latency regression (5-10%) on the decoder-heavy workloads after yesterday's scheduler tweak. Traces point to a new slowpath during batch formation. anyone else seeing this?
ajay: saw it in the canary graphs around 18:40 UTC. p50 fine, p95 bump on gen-heavy flows.
linh: I pulled a perf profile, attaching quick snippet of flame: kernel-switch spikes when batch size oscillates between 1-4 tokens during decode. looks like kernel selection thrashes between small/large-kernel paths.
maria: interesting — could be the continuous-batcher heuristic that tries to pack prefill+decode, then rebalances mid-gen.
devon: also saw KV cache churn on the same hosts. decode microbatches evict prefills' KV pages, causing extra priming on next prefill.
kevin: that eviction would increase cold-start decode costs — matches the trace.
ajay: hypothesis: the handshake window and token_budget target are too permissive, letting very short decode microbatches run on the heavy kernel path then bounce to light kernel, causing overhead.
linh: agreed. two levers: 1) make prefill and decode queue admission separate (so decode short tails don't evict prefill entries), 2) introduce a small stable-hold for kernel choice so we don't flip for very small deltas.
maria: can we try a quick config patch on canary? maybe reduce decode token_budget target from 32 to 12 and increase handshake_window from 4ms to 12ms. that should bias short decodes to stay in a consistent kernel.
ajay: sounds reasonable. devon — can you spin canary with these knobs? config snippet below: 
```json
{"continuous_batcher": {"decode_token_budget": 12, "handshake_window_ms": 12, "prefill_queue_isolation": true}}
```
devon: yeah I can roll that. will also enable kv-priming-guard: hold last-primed-session for 250ms to reduce eviction.
kevin: add a metric: kernel_switch_rate (switches/sec per host) + kv_eviction_rate. alert if kernel_switch_rate > 0.5 and p95 increases.
linh: I instrumented a tiny benchmark — synthetic short-decode stream. baseline kernel_switch_rate ~0.9, with token_budget=12 -> ~0.15, p95 down ~7%. promising.
maria: nice. let's run canary for 30m and compare cost/latency. canary hosts: infra-canary-4/5.
ajay: one more thought: for models with very short decode tokens (<8 tokens) we may want to always use compact-kernel variant regardless of batch size. add as a model-level hint.
linh: I can add a small mapping table: model_hint_short_decode = ["redwood-mini","bert-lite"]; runtime will prioritize compact kernel when hint present.
devon: rolling patch now to infra-canary-4. will post results.
perf-bot: deploy started: change-id=CL12345 by devon to infra-canary-4 at 2026-03-20T18:55:10Z 
maria: thanks. if canary looks good, we'll stage to canary-5 then ramp. also open to lowering prefill queue eviction threshold temporarily.
kevin: FYI I'm on-call — ping me if p95 gets worse after traffic ramp.
devon: canary done, initial 10min window looks cleaner: kernel_switch_rate down to 0.2, kv_eviction_rate down ~30%.
ajay: great. let's keep these changes behind a rollout flag and add regression test: synthetic short-decode flood that measures kernel_switch_rate and kv misses.
linh: I'll add perf regression harness and a visual to the console (per-route kernel stability).
maria: plan: 1) keep canary 30m, 2) if stable, roll to 20% for 1h, monitor kernel_switch_rate & p95, 3) follow with model_hint table and longer kv-priming guard.
kevin: +1. also add alert on kv_eviction_rate delta > 15% vs baseline.
ajay: capturing action items: devon roll, linh perf harness + hint table, maria coordinate rollout, kevin alerting.
maria: thanks team. next update in ~30m.
devon: update @30m: canary at 30min still looks good, p95 back to baseline, cost delta trivial. will start 20% ramp in 10m.
perf-bot: canary ramp: 20% started at 2026-03-20T19:35:42Z
